literal_meaning: বিদ্যায় বৃহস্পতি (knowledge in Brihaspati, where Brihaspati is the divine guru)
figurative_meaning_en: Sarcastically referring to someone with superficial or little knowledge
similar_in_english: A little knowledge is a dangerous thing
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে বিদ্যায় বৃহস্পতি বলে মনে করে, কিন্তু আসলে তার জ্ঞান অতি সামান্য।
এই বিষয়ে তার বিদ্যায় বৃহস্পতি হয়ে গেছে, তাই কথা শোনা উচিত নয়।
example_sentences_in_english: He thinks he's Brihaspati in knowledge, but his understanding is very superficial.
In this matter, he's become a Brihaspati of sorts, so his advice should be ignored.
history: References Brihaspati (Jupiter), the preceptor of the gods in Hindu mythology, used ironically to mock pretentious ignorance.
note: The idiom draws from mythological reverence to highlight false expertise.
